abstract: By utilizing the staggered implementation of China’s low-carbon city pilot (LCCP) policies, we show that firms exposed to carbon risk will reduce corporate environmental disclosure. The negative effect is stronger when firms face more external pressure to meet carbon reduction targets. The negative effect can be mitigated by external monitors, and for firms with greater real environmental investment, more attention and more responsibility for carbon emission reduction. Lower corporate environmental disclosure may further lead to a deterioration of the stock price informativeness. Our findings shed light on the unintended consequences of policies that expose firms to higher carbon risk. For government and regulatory institutions, these results provide valuable insights for the need to complement carbon reduction policies with targeted guidance on environmental information disclosure, strengthen the supervision and incentive mechanisms that align firms’ real environmental investment with transparent disclosure.

title: Green-hushing: unintended consequences of carbon risk on corporate environmental disclosure
